format.description: The version of this file format. Always 1.

id.description: A name for this figure, like "hero". It matches the file name.

tile.description: How many pixels of the picture make one tile of the game, in pixels.

w.description: How wide one pose is, in pixels.

h.description: How tall one pose is, in pixels.

frame.description: The size of one pose, in pixels.

outline.description: An edge one pixel wide round the whole figure, as # and six digits, like #111314. Left out means no edge.

id.description: A name for this colour, for what it is for, like "body", "trim" or "ink".

color.description: The colour, as # and six digits, like #f37f94.

paints.description: The colours the parts use, each named for what it is for.

id.description: A name for this part, used once in this figure, like "head".

shape.description: "block" is a rectangle; "round" is an ellipse that fills the same box.

x.description: Where the part's middle is, in pixels from the left edge of the frame.

y.description: Where the part's middle is, in pixels from the top edge of the frame.

w.description: How wide the part is, in pixels.

h.description: How tall the part is, in pixels.

paint.description: Which of the figure's paints it is drawn in, by id, like "body".

turn.description: How far it is turned clockwise about its middle, in degrees. Left out means not turned.

parts.description: The parts, drawn first to last, so the first is at the back.

id.description: A name for this pose, used once in this figure, like "idle" or "run-1".

part.description: Which part moves, by id, like "head".

dx.description: How far it moves right (left if below 0), in pixels. Left out means not at all.

dy.description: How far it moves down (up if below 0), in pixels. Left out means not at all.

turn.description: How much further it turns clockwise, in degrees, added to the part's own. Left out means none.

moves.description: The parts that move in this pose. Write [] for the figure just as its parts say.

poses.description: The ways the figure can stand. Each one is a picture in the figure's sheet.

id.description: A name for these colours, used once in this figure, like "two".
A name for this colour, for what it is for, like "body", "trim" or "ink".

color.description: The colour, as # and six digits, like #f37f94.

paints.description: Only the paints that change, each with the id it has in the figure and its new colour.

variants.description: The same figure in other colours. Player 2's hero is drawn in the first, player 3's in the second, player 4's in the third. Left out means none.
